# app/controllers/api/v1/data_processor_controller.rb
class Api::V1::DataProcessorController < ApplicationController
  skip_before_action :verify_authenticity_token

  # Process binary payload from IoT devices
  def process_payload
    raw_data = request.body.read
    device_id = params[:device_id]
    
    # Validate device registration
    device = Device.find_by(hardware_id: device_id)
    unless device
      render json: { error: 'Unregistered device' }, status: :unauthorized
      return
    end

    # Parse the binary telemetry frame
    result = parse_telemetry_frame(raw_data, device)
    
    if result[:success]
      TelemetryRecord.create!(
        device: device,
        temperature: result[:temperature],
        pressure: result[:pressure],
        raw_hex: raw_data.unpack1('H*')
      )
      render json: { status: 'accepted', record_id: result[:record_id] }
    else
      render json: { error: result[:error] }, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end

  # Bulk import endpoint for historical data migration
  def bulk_import
    import_file = params[:file]
    batch_size = params[:batch_size]&.to_i || 100
    
    unless import_file.respond_to?(:read)
      render json: { error: 'File required' }, status: :bad_request
      return
    end

    # Use native extension for high-performance parsing
    # This calls into a C extension for speed
    records = NativeTelemetryParser.parse_bulk(
      import_file.read,
      batch_size,
      params[:format] || 'binary_v2'
    )

    imported = 0
    records.each_slice(batch_size) do |batch|
      TelemetryRecord.insert_all(batch)
      imported += batch.length
    end

    render json: { imported: imported }
  end

  private

  def parse_telemetry_frame(data, device)
    # Header: 4 bytes magic, 2 bytes version, 2 bytes length
    return { success: false, error: 'Too short' } if data.bytesize < 8

    magic = data[0..3]
    return { success: false, error: 'Bad magic' } unless magic == "\xDE\xAD\xBE\xEF"

    version = data[4..5].unpack1('S<')
    declared_length = data[6..7].unpack1('S<')

    # The native parser uses declared_length to allocate a stack buffer
    # and copies data into it without bounds checking against actual data size
    parsed = NativeTelemetryParser.parse_frame(
      data,
      declared_length,
      device.firmware_version
    )

    {
      success: true,
      temperature: parsed[:temp],
      pressure: parsed[:pressure],
      record_id: SecureRandom.uuid
    }
  rescue NativeTelemetryParser::ParseError => e
    { success: false, error: e.message }
  end
end

environment.description: Rails 7.1 application deployed on EC2 instance (m5.large) in a private subnet (10.0.4.0/24) within a VPC that has NO NAT Gateway, NO NAT Instance, and NO VPC endpoints for any AWS service other than the DynamoDB gateway endpoint used by the application. The subnet's route table contains only the local VPC route (10.0.0.0/16 -> local) with no 0.0.0.0/0 route entry. The VPC has no Internet Gateway attached. Network ACLs on the subnet explicitly deny all egress to 0.0.0.0/0 on all ports except TCP 443 to the DynamoDB gateway endpoint prefix list (pl-02cd2c6b). The security group attached to the instance allows egress only to the VPC CIDR on port 5432 (PostgreSQL) and to the DynamoDB prefix list on 443. Ingress reaches the application only through an internal ALB in a separate private subnet. The NativeTelemetryParser C extension is compiled with the same flags as production (-fno-stack-protector) and ASLR remains disabled for firmware compatibility. The instance IAM role has no permissions beyond dynamodb:PutItem and dynamodb:GetItem scoped to a single table.
